done_when: Reproduce it (run the two tests in a loop under load on macOS), name the root cause with evidence, fix it at the cause so forge work never returns while a Codex process it started is alive, and both tests pass on every OS in CI three runs in a row; no test is skipped or loosened

dismissals.because: src/forge/codex.py:260 Forge has already sent SIGKILL to the whole process group it created and waited 30 seconds; SIGKILL can't be caught or ignored, so a process still alive is stuck in the kernel, and refusing loudly is the right fail-closed answer rather than hanging forge work forever

findings.body: The timeout still allows `forge work` to return while its app-server remains alive. After 300 successful probes, `repo.refuse()` raises an exception; `src/forge/cli.py:173-175` catches it and exits. Returning an error does not satisfy the requirement that Forge never returns with a surviving Codex process. In the bare-command scenario this patch targets, the outer cleanup cannot repair this: `src/forge/codex.py:371-372` skips that app-server record, including during `hold()` cleanup at line 420. Keep ownership and wait for confirmed termination before exiting, and add coverage for termination outlasting the polling budget.
